description:
## Goal

Create the controlled Tauri listener test harness and prove the App lifecycle when the stale StrictMode setup completes both registrations before the live setup.

**Triage:** ready-for-agent

## Background and relevant code

PR #55 made `src/App.tsx:181-274` subscription-first. Under `React.StrictMode` (`src/main.tsx:16-18`), setup 1 starts listener registration, cleanup 1 marks its closure-local `disposed_1` true, and setup 2 starts a separate registration flow with `disposed_2` false.

`src/App.tsx:192-216` registers transition and then refresh sequentially. The stale setup must immediately invoke late unlisten handles at `src/App.tsx:199-203` and `211-215`; its outer check at `src/App.tsx:264-266` must suppress startup. The live setup must retain its handles and call `dispatchStartupLoad()` at `src/App.tsx:267` only after both registrations finish.

Existing `createBothListenersMock()` in `src/test/app-workspace-fixtures.ts:51-74` resolves immediately and cannot control StrictMode completion ordering. Existing App mocks in `src/App.issue-refresh.test.tsx:18-103` are the pattern to reuse.

## Work

Prefer a focused `src/App.strict-mode-lifecycle.test.tsx`. Build a test-only controller for mocked `listen(eventName, callback)` that:

- returns a manually controlled promise;
- records the event name and callback when App requests registration;
- assigns logical names `T1`, `T2`, `R1`, and `R2` based on the two StrictMode setups and event type;
- provides one unlisten spy per registration;
- can resolve one named registration at a time;
- exposes active registrations or enough spy state to prove ownership;
- fails clearly if a refresh registration is resolved before App has requested it.

Render the real App as:

```tsx
<React.StrictMode>
  <App />
</React.StrictMode>
```

Resolve registrations in stale-first order:

```text
T1 → R1 → T2 → R2
```

Use `act(async () => ...)` around resolution/flush operations. Before `R2` resolves, assert startup has not begun. After all continuations settle, assert:

- `T1` and `R1` unlisten exactly once;
- `T2` and `R2` remain active while mounted;
- `listen` was called four times: two transition and two refresh registrations;
- `loadIssueExplorerStateFromTauRpc()` ran exactly once;
- TauRPC `workspace_state()` ran exactly once;
- no stale or duplicate startup appears after another microtask flush.

## Design notes

Each setup has a separate local boolean. The test should fail if production changes to a shared ref that setup 2 resets, because stale run 1 would then retain its handles or dispatch startup.

Keep the immediate listener helper used by ordinary behavior tests simple. Put the deferred controller in the focused test file unless later child tasks justify a shared test helper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The harness drives the real imported `App`, not a copied listener algorithm.
- [ ] Registration promises are manually controlled and named by lifecycle/event.
- [ ] Refresh registration is observed only after the matching transition resolves.
- [ ] Stale-first ordering removes `T1`/`R1` exactly once.
- [ ] Live `T2`/`R2` remain active before unmount.
- [ ] Startup Issue and Workspace reads each run exactly once and only after `R2`.
- [ ] No timers, sleeps, act warnings, or unhandled rejections.
- [ ] Focused App lifecycle test passes.
- [ ] Existing `src/App.issue-refresh.test.tsx` remains green.
- [ ] `pnpm check` passes.
title: Test stale-first App listener registration under StrictMode
